title: "what else is like this" is used by people other than the member it belongs to
summary: "what else is like this" is the caption @norvid-studies.bsky.social puts on quote-posts to ask for more examples of the thing quoted. In this window other people used it in the same way, and some turned it on him. Members quote-posted a study about crows' decision speed and a post about a monitor left at 12 percent brightness with only those five words, and got examples back in the replies. When @spacecowboy17.bsky.social announced a feed that shows what else the people who liked a post have liked (Sun 15 Nov, 220 likes), the first reply, one minute later and from a non-member, was a tag of @norvid-studies.bsky.social with the phrase; the next day a member wrote that they had pinned "the 'what else is like this' feed". In that thread and elsewhere the phrase is paired with "claim", another one-word caption used in the cluster. One member proposed "a jev" (the cluster's word for a small bot) that sorts every post into the two, and another member's talking toy has a "claim mode" in which it asks the question aloud.

* press any key to power on
* spell a word or phrase with letters and/or space
* press "prompt" to say it
* press "repeat" to say last one again
* "claim" is a toggle for a special "claim mode"
* in "claim mode" you can prompt to ask "what else is like this"

numbers: My count from posts.jsonl (case-insensitive match of the five words, 13 Nov 00:00Z to 19 Nov 09:54Z): 34 posts by 18 accounts, 16 of them cluster members, on all seven days. 13 of the 34 are by @norvid-studies.bsky.social; no other account has more than 2.
Counts as of the digest: the monitor quote-post 64 likes and 9 replies; the crows quote-post 36 likes; the feed announcement 220 likes, 36 reposts, 12 quotes.
couldBeShown: The feed is a working thing with a public description of what it does (the made lane may card it). The talking toy's user guide is listed here only for its "claim mode" lines.
notUnderstood: Where "claim" as a caption comes from, beyond its use in these posts. What image @norvid-studies.bsky.social attached to "to quote @croissanthology.com" (no alt text). What "a jev" is exactly: members use it as a common noun for a small model or bot of the kind run at @jevbot.bsky.social; I did not find its operator or how it works.
sensitive: No post on this card carries a flag from the tool. (1) @norvid-studies.bsky.social is marked by the tool as having spoken in the previous episode: his posts may be shown, his puppet does not speak. The phrase is his; this card is about other people using it, and 21 of the 34 uses are not his. (2) Five uses of the phrase in the window are flagged by the tool post by post (health; grief and disaster) and two more sit inside stories the digest flags; all seven are left out, including the most-liked use, from outside the cluster (236 likes). (3) Also left out as unclear or near the line: a use that quotes a joke about God and an insect's brain, a follow-up I could not place ("The Vitamin"), and a reply about first getting glasses (health-adjacent). (4) @satyrs.eu (402 followers), @kyefox.com (4,685) and the two quoted accounts (@obialik.bsky.social, @ari.express) are outside the cluster's membership; the crows post is a science writer's, quoted as the occasion only. (5) "One cannot gate-keep a simcluster." was said in play, in reply to a joke about a bot; it is not a statement of principle by its author and cannot be presented as one (R4). (6) @shimmermathlabs.com is marked as shown in the previous episode; @spacecowboy17.bsky.social has 5,812 followers and @eva.computer 18,063.
